qwen3.8-flash-next.notes: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next multimodal MoE, the Qwen4 architecture preview (HF model_type 'qwen4_exp', GGUF arch 'qwen4exp'): 125B total / 6B activated parameters plus 51B n-gram embedding (bigram/trigram lookup at layer 2) and a 4B 1-layer MTP head; 48 layers laid out as 12 x (3 x (Gated DeltaNet -> MoE) then 1 x (Qwen Sparse Attention -> MoE)), i.e. full_attention_interval 4, with QSA selecting micro-blocks under a 2048-token indexer budget; MoE is 512 routed experts + 1 shared with 10 activated; gated residual streams (4 branches, rank 320). Native context 262,144 tokens, extensible to 1,000,000 via static YaRN (set factor 4.0 in text_config.rope_parameters; the shipped config has rope_type 'default'). Thinking is ON by default (disable per request with chat_template_kwargs enable_thinking=false); depth is tuned with reasoning_effort (xhigh default, medium, low; the template aliases 'high' to 'xhigh') and prior reasoning is retained via preserve_thinking (on by default). Tool calls use the Qwen3-Coder XML convention (<tool_call><function=name><parameter=key> blocks) taught directly by the chat template. max_output_tokens records the card's FINAL-response budget (131,072); the card additionally recommends up to 262,144 tokens for reasoning content on frameworks that cap reasoning separately. inference_parameters record the thinking-mode sampling defaults (also embedded in the GGUF); for non-thinking use the card recommends temperature=0.7, top_p=0.8, top_k=20, presence_penalty=1.5. GGUF inference requires llama.cpp with 'qwen4exp' support (ggml-org/llama.cpp PR #27742, still unmerged as of 2026-08-27; llama-cpp-python <= 0.3.35 and LM Studio engine <= 2.29.1 cannot load it).

Unified model for reasoning and non-reasoning tasks with configurable reasoning mode. Generates reasoning trace before final response. nemotron-3-nano-4b.notes: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Nano 4B edge SLM (3.97B params). DENSE hybrid Mamba-2/MLP architecture with only four attention layers, compressed from Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2 via Nemotron Elastic. Unlike the 30B/120B siblings it is NOT mixture-of-experts; it shares the nemotron_hybrid_moe registry architecture only for chat-format/thinking-control purposes (im_start_end, XML <tool_call>, <think></think> tags). Reasoning is enabled by default via the enable_thinking chat-template kwarg (template default True; truncate_history_thinking also supported); when disabled the generation prompt pre-fills an empty <think></think>. Thinking-on generation prompts open an unclosed <think>, so decoded output may contain reasoning terminated only by </think> (closing-only capture) or no tags at all depending on the serving template. LM Studio (2026-07-07) returned no separate reasoning field and no think tags, and enable_thinking:false showed no measurable suppression on that endpoint. Model card recommends temperature 1.0/top_p 0.95 for reasoning and 0.6/0.95 for tool calling; vLLM serving uses tool parser qwen3_coder and the nano_v3 reasoning parser plugin with max-model-len up to 262144. No hard completion cap published; 8192 mirrors the sibling nemotron-3-nano-30b-a3b registry convention.

Thinking effort levels: non-thinking / High / Max (Max mapped to xhigh). Function calling and structured outputs exposed by the Z.ai API and vLLM/SGLang parsers. glm-5.3.notes: GLM-5.3 frontier coding flagship (launch coverage dates the API 2026-08-14 and the open weights 2026-08-28 after a safety hold; the Hugging Face repo was created 2026-08-25 and Z.ai publishes no date; released under the bespoke GLM-5.3 license rather than MIT). HF config: GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM / model_type glm_moe_dsa, 78 layers, hidden size 6144, 256 routed + 1 shared experts with 8 activated, one MTP layer, max_position_embeddings 1,048,576, FP8 weights (BF16 in zai-org/GLM-5.3-BF16). Z.ai API: text-only input, 1M-token context, 128K max output, function calling and JSON structured output; reasoning is always on (thinking.type accepts only enabled, disabled fails the request), reasoning_effort low|high|max with default max (max is not in the unified thinking vocabulary, see max_effort_supported); the chat template's clear_thinking defaults to false. Because thinking cannot be turned off, thinking_control is deliberately absent. Z.ai pricing $1.40 input, $0.26 cached input, $4.40 output per MTok. Evaluation sampling on the card: temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95.

HF config: Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration / model_type glm5_next (text glm5_next_text, vision glm5_next_vision), 45 layers, hidden size 4096, 288 routed + 1 shared experts with 8 activated, hybrid sparse + linear attention with Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections, one MTP layer, max_position_embeddings 1,048,576, FP8 weights (BF16 in zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash-BF16). Chat conventions follow the GLM-5 family (architecture_formats glm5_dsa pattern), while the registry records the true HF model_type here. Z.ai API (glm-5.3-flash, and glm-5.3-flashx with identical weights served at up to 200 tokens/s): video, image, text and file input, text output, 1M context, 128K max output, function calling (tool_stream recommended when streaming) and JSON structured output; thinking.type accepts only enabled, recommended reasoning_effort max; the Flash page lists no other values, so low|high|max is carried over from the GLM-5.3 page (max is not in the unified vocabulary, see max_effort_supported) and thinking.clear_thinking false; thinking_control is deliberately absent because thinking cannot be turned off. Z.ai pricing $0.15/$0.50 per MTok (cached input $0.03); FlashX $0.37/$1.25. Recommended sampling temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95.

hy-memory-30b-a3b.notes: Specialty seems to be a long-term memory writer: Tencent Hunyuan trained it to execute the WRITE path inside external memory frameworks (drop-in writer LLM for Mem0, MemOS and Hy-Memory; transfers to EverMemOS) — deciding what to retain, how precisely to represent it and how new evidence updates the memory bank. HYV3ForCausalLM (model_type 'hy_v3'): 48 layers, hidden 2048, GQA 32 heads / 4 KV heads (head_dim 128, QK-norm), layer 0 dense (intermediate 6912), layers 1-47 MoE with 128 routed experts (8 activated) + 1 shared expert, sigmoid router with selection-only expert bias, route_norm and router_scaling_factor 2.826; no MTP layers; 120,832-token vocab; default RoPE (theta 11,158,840); config max_position_embeddings 262,144. CHECKPOINT QUIRK: routed and shared expert tensors are 768 wide (config 'expert_hidden_dim': 768) while config 'moe_intermediate_size' says 1536, which is what transformers' hy_v3 (5.8) reads — loaders must size experts from expert_hidden_dim. Chat template: BOS then bare system text, <｜hy_User｜>/<｜hy_Assistant｜>, eos <eos:6124c78e>; ONE 'reasoning_effort' template variable (high | low | no_think; unset or unknown renders no_think, so thinking is OFF by default; no_think pre-closes an empty <think></think> after the assistant token, low/high open <think>). Tool calls: <tool_calls><tool_call>name<tool_sep><arg_key>k</arg_key><arg_value>v</arg_value></tool_call></tool_calls> (non-string values JSON-encoded); tool results in <tool_responses><tool_response>. Card quickstart: vLLM (tested v0.31.0), chat_template_kwargs {"reasoning_effort": "no_think"}, temperature 0.0 and max_tokens 512 for memory extraction; the GGUF card's llama-server defaults are --temp 0.7 --top-k 0 --top-p 1.0 --repeat-penalty 1.0 --jinja with reasoning_effort no_think (inference_parameters mirror temp/top_p; top_k 0 = disabled is left to the backend). No output cap is published: max_output_tokens 16,384 leaves room for a reasoning_effort=high trace plus the memory payload while bounding runaway local generations — raise per deployment. Artifacts: tencent BF16 safetensors (51 shards, 60.1 GB), tencent FP8 (F8_E4M3, vLLM/SGLang only — no Apple-silicon path), tencent GGUF (Q4_K_M-imat 18.2 GB, Q6_K-imat 24.7 GB, Q8_0 32 GB; llama.cpp arch hy_v3), and mlx-community 4-bit / 8-bit MLX conversions that bundle the model class (hy_v3.py via config 'model_file') because mlx-lm ships no hy_v3 module. Paper arXiv 2610.22196; code github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/Hy-Memory.
hy-memory-30b-a3b.source: Hugging Face model cards, config.json, tokenizer.json, chat_template.jinja and safetensors index (tencent/Hy-Memory-30B-A3B @64a460a9, tencent/Hy-Memory-30B-A3B-FP8, tencent/Hy-Memory-30B-A3B-GGUF; HF API createdAt 2026-10-15), accessed 2026-10-21

minimax-m3.1-flash.notes: MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, the efficient successor of MiniMax-M3 (GA on the MiniMax platform 2026-10-19 as MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, preceded by a MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview inside MiniMax Code per press coverage; open weights announced for 2026-10-23). Keeps M3's MoE (about 428B total / 23B activated; config: 60 layers, hidden size 6144, 128 routed + 1 shared experts with 4 activated, MiniMaxM3SparseForConditionalGeneration / model_type minimax_m3_vl) with three changes: the first three full-attention layers become MiniMax Sparse Attention, routed experts and attention paths are quantization-aware trained (shipped checkpoint: mxfp8 weights with nvfp4-packed experts), and DSpark replaces the EAGLE-style MTP head for speculative decoding. 1,048,576-token context (config), text, image and video input, text output, CLIP vision tower at 672 px. Reasoning depth is set with reasoning_effort low|medium|high|xhigh|max in the chat template (max is not in the unified thinking vocabulary, see max_effort_supported); thinking tags follow the M3 family (<mm:think>). No completion cap is published, so max_output_tokens is null. Card sampling temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95. Platform price $0.15/$0.60 per MTok, cache reads $0.015. License minimax-community.

Thinking toggled with the chat-template kwarg enable_thinking (the API examples pass it explicitly as true) and a medium_effort=true kwarg for fewer reasoning tokens; a client-side reasoning_budget example caps the trace. Tool calls via the qwen3_coder parser (vLLM --enable-auto-tool-choice, SGLang needs force_nonempty_content with tools), reasoning parser nemotron_v3 / nano-v3. Examples use temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95. Hosted as nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b on build.nvidia.com (the card's API example uses the served name nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra). The config's max_position_embeddings is 262,144; the 1M figure is the card's stated ceiling. OpenMDW License 1.1. No completion cap published; 8,192 mirrors the sibling Nemotron 3 registry convention.

nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b.notes: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (GA 2026-08-11): 30B total / 3B active hybrid MoE (interleaved Mamba-2 and MoE layers, select attention layers, MTP layers, NVFP4 pre-training recipe); text in, text out; English plus Spanish, French, German, Italian, Japanese and code; up to 1M-token context per the card (256K on one H100 in BF16; the config's max_position_embeddings is 262,144). Thinking on by default, toggled with the chat-template kwarg enable_thinking; coding agents should pass force_nonempty_content=true. Tool calls via the qwen3_coder parser (vLLM --enable-auto-tool-choice; SGLang reasoning parser nemotron_3). Card sampling temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95. Speculative decoding through the separate NVFP4-DSpark and NVFP4-DFlash draft repos (not aliased here). Beats Nemotron 3 Nano on SWE-bench Verified (51.56 vs 34.08). OpenMDW License 1.1. No completion cap published; 8,192 mirrors the Nemotron 3 registry convention.

nemotron-3.5-bolt-74b-a9b.notes: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B (released 2026-10-15): 74B total / 9B active Mamba2-Transformer hybrid MoE derived from the Nemotron 3.5 Super backbone by an architecture search (expert top-k 9, down from 22; per-layer routed-expert counts and MoE widths) with a C-RADIO v4-H vision encoder and MLP projector. Input text, images (JPEG/PNG) and video (MP4 up to 2 minutes, up to 1 fps / 128 frames at 1080p); text output; up to 256K tokens shared by prompt, images, history, tool results and output. Thinking via chat_template_kwargs enable_thinking true/false plus medium_effort=true; reasoning and answer share max_tokens. Tool calls via the qwen3_coder parser, reasoning parser ultra_v3 plugin; JSON output listed as supported. Text sampling temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95. The 24GB repos are native 2-bit quantizations sized to run beside other applications in 24 GB (search target below 24 GB at batch 1 and 128K context); the BF16 release is meant for post-training rather than production inference. OpenMDW-1.1.

nemotron-3.5-bolt-e4b.notes: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B (released 2026-10-23): an 8B (4B effective) model on the Gemma-4-E4B architecture for fast local voice/device assistants and edge interfaces (Jetson Orin/Thor, DGX Spark, RTX). Text in, text out per the card (the repo tag says image-text-to-text, but the card lists text only, so no vision is declared); input up to 64K tokens and output up to 64K tokens. Thinking via enable_thinking=true/false plus a runtime thinking budget and a conversational_mode toggle. Native tools array with the gemma4 parser on vLLM (--enable-auto-tool-choice). Sampling temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95 in both modes. The 4GB repo is the Q4_K_M GGUF; a companion DFlash drafter exists for speculative decoding (not aliased). OpenMDW-1.1 (base Gemma 4 under Apache-2.0). Registry architecture gemma4 because the chat template is Gemma 4's, not the Nemotron hybrid one.

nemotron-3.5-super-vl-120b-a12b.notes: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL (released 2026-10-15): 120B total / 12B active hybrid MoE (interleaved Mamba-2, MoE and attention layers; 512 routed experts per MoE layer) with a C-RADIO vision encoder and vision-language connector. Input text, images (jpeg/png), video (mp4 up to 2 minutes) and documents as page images; text output; up to 1M-token context. Thinking via enable_thinking true/false with a medium level through medium_effort=true. Tool calls via the OpenAI-compatible tools parameter with the qwen3_coder parser (vLLM --enable-auto-tool-choice), reasoning parser nemotron_v3 / nemotron_3. Card sampling: text temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95; vision 0.6/0.95. OpenMDW-1.1. No completion cap published; 8,192 mirrors the Nemotron 3 registry convention.

nemotron-nano-9b-v2.notes: NVIDIA Nemotron Nano 9B v2 (released 2025-08-18): 9B dense Mamba2-Transformer hybrid (Nemotron-Hybrid) made mostly of Mamba-2 and MLP layers with four attention layers; text in, text out; up to 128K-token input and output. Reasoning is toggled with /think or /no_think in the system prompt (default on when no signal is given) and per turn in user messages; budget control with max_thinking_tokens (soft stop at the next newline, hard cut at budget + 500). Tool calls are a JSON list of name/arguments objects inside <TOOLCALL> tags with results in <TOOL_RESPONSE> (vLLM parser nemotron_json), so the registry tool format is json, not the XML of the Nemotron 3 family that shares its architecture block. Card sampling: reasoning on temperature 0.6, top_p 0.95; reasoning off greedy; max_new_tokens 1,024 or more with reasoning. NVIDIA Open Model License. The 12B sibling is NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-12B-v2.

nemotron-nano-12b-v2-vl.notes: NVIDIA Nemotron Nano 12B v2 VL (released 2025-10-28): 12.6B multimodal document-intelligence model pairing the NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-12B-v2 hybrid language backbone with the CRadioV2-H vision encoder; input + output 128K tokens; English text. Images: up to 4 per request, minimum 32x32 px, tiled into up to 12 tiles of 512x512 (e.g. 2048x1536). Video: the model takes pre-extracted frames at 2 fps (8 to 128 frames; MP4/MKV/FLV/3GP must be decoded by the caller), so video is frame-based here. Examples use a '/no_think' system message and greedy decoding (max_new_tokens 1,024 for images, 128 for video); function calling appears only as a training dataset, so tool support is treated as prompted. NVIDIA Open Model License.

nemotron-3-embed-1b.notes: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Embed 1B (released 2026-07-16): about 1.14B-parameter text embedding model pruned from Ministral-3-3B-Instruct-2512, bidirectional attention with average pooling, distilled from Nemotron-3-Embed-8B; 2048-dim vectors that can be sliced to 1024 or 512 and re-normalized; max sequence length 32,768 (evaluated at 4,096); 34 languages. Prefix queries with 'query: ' and documents with 'passage: ' (vLLM /v2/embed applies them via input_type). Not a text-generative model. OpenMDW-1.1.

nemotron-3.5-embed-1b.notes: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Embed 1B (released 2026-10-20): 1.55B-parameter multimodal retrieval embedder, a Pixtral vision encoder from Ministral-3-3B-Instruct-2512 on the Nemotron-3-Embed-1B language model. Queries are text only; documents can be an image (default longest edge 1,120 px, up to 1,540), text, or image plus text (visual-document retrieval); 2048-dim vectors sliceable to 1024 or 512; max context 32,768 tokens. Prefix queries with 'query: ' and documents with 'passage: ' (vLLM input_type). Not a text-generative model. OpenMDW-1.1; an 8B sibling exists.

nemotron-3.5-transcribe-30b-a4b.notes: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe (released 2026-10-28): 34B total / 4.3B active speech model, a roughly 600M transformer ASR encoder plus a 99M speaker encoder (Nemotron-3-Diarization) on the Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B-A3B Mamba-2/Transformer MoE backbone. Input 16 kHz mono audio (wav/flac/mp3/ogg, anything decodable to PCM) up to one hour; 65,536-token context. Output text with optional word timestamps, speaker tags and diarization segments (ctc_timestamps), and translation between English and the supported languages; 40 languages. Served through vLLM 0.32+ with NeMo Speech (OpenAI-compatible), NeMo ASRModel.transcribe, SGLang-Omni /v1/audio/transcriptions, or Transformers AutoModelForMultimodalLM; FP8 and NVFP4 post-training quantized variants; a separate DFlash2 draft model. The card lists a configurable reasoning mode through the chat template (enable_thinking true/false); no tool calling. OpenMDW-1.1.

nemotron-3.5-parse.notes: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Parse (released 2026-10-17; DFlash2 speculative-decoding update 2026-11-04): about 0.63B-parameter document parser, C-RADIOv4-SO400M vision encoder (vit_so400m_patch16_224, dynamic rectangular NaViT preprocessing, 1D-convolution adapter) with a 10-layer mBART causal visual-prefix decoder (16 query / 8 KV heads) and one MTP head; optional 89.3M DFlash2 drafter. Input: RGB page images (render PDFs first, e.g. 150 DPI) up to 1664x2048 plus a task prompt; output: text with semantic classes, normalized bounding boxes and reading order, Markdown with HTML tables, convertible to LaTeX/HTML/Markdown/JSON/CSV; examples use max_new_tokens 8,744 and the config states max_position_embeddings 16,384. ParseBench 75.20 vs 63.91 for Parse 2.0. Served with Transformers (trust_remote_code), vLLM (--speculative-config for DFlash2), SGLang, the NVIDIA Build API or Baseten. No chat or tool calling. OpenMDW-1.1 (tokenizer MIT).

nemotron-parse-2.0.notes: NVIDIA Nemotron Parse 2.0 (released 2026-08-03): sub-1B (0.9B) vision-encoder-decoder document parser, C-RADIO ViT-H encoder, 1D-convolution adapter and an mBART decoder (10 blocks per the card; the config's decoder num_hidden_layers is 12) with a 72,256-entry vocabulary (about 20K tokens added over v1.2, including a <class_Chart> token for chart-aware parsing). Input: an RGB document image (recommended 1024x1280 to 1664x2048) plus a task prompt, default '</s><s><predict_bbox><predict_classes><output_markdown><predict_no_text_in_pic>'; output: text with element classes and bounding boxes, convertible to LaTeX/HTML/Markdown/JSON/CSV; examples use max_tokens 8,192 to 9,000 and no context length is stated (16,384 recorded as a serving-sized window). ParseBench 0.6391 vs 0.5782 for v1.2; superseded by Nemotron-3.5-Parse. No chat or tool calling. OpenMDW-1.1 (tokenizer CC-BY-4.0).

laguna-s-2.1.notes: Poolside Laguna-S-2.1 agentic-coding MoE (LagunaForCausalLM, model_type 'laguna'; 48 layers, 256 routed + 1 shared experts, 10 routed activated per token; 100,352-token vocab). Attention interleaves 12 global (YaRN, factor 128) and 36 sliding-window layers (window 512) with 8 KV heads. Config max_position_embeddings 1,048,576 (1M context). Native tool calling and reasoning via the 'poolside_v1' parsers in vLLM/SGLang (TRT-LLM uses reasoning parser 'laguna'); thinking is interleaved between tool calls and enabled by default, disabled per request with chat_template_kwargs {"enable_thinking": false}. Tool calls use the GLM-style <tool_call>name<arg_key>k</arg_key><arg_value>v</arg_value></tool_call> encoding; stop tokens are 〈|EOS|〉 and </assistant>. Model card states no separate output-token cap, so max_output_tokens is a practical serving default bounded by the 1M context. Siblings: Laguna-XS-2.1 / XS.2 / M.1, plus FP8, NVFP4, INT4, GGUF and MLX quantizations and DFlash speculative-decoding draft models.

ernie-5.5-flash-base.notes: Baidu ERNIE-5.5-Flash-Base, the text-only MoE BASE checkpoint at the end of pre-training (no mid- or post-training, no chat template, served through the completions endpoint): 280B total / 14B activated, 43 layers (1 dense FFN + 42 Multi-Router Latent MoE), 512 routed experts top-10 plus 1 shared per MoE layer (latent and expert dim 2048), 37 Heavily Compressed Attention (HCA) layers and 6 MLA layers with 64 heads; HF config Ernie5_5_MoeForCausalLM / model_type ernie5_5_moe, hidden size 4096, YaRN factor 16 over 65,536 original positions to max_position_embeddings 1,048,576 (card: 128K max training context, 1M for fine-tuning and inference). Main repo FP8 (e4m3, 128x128 blocks); ERNIE-5.5-Flash-Base-BF16 is the BF16 variant. As a base model it has no thinking mode, tool calling or structured-output protocol. Adds SR-SWA (a fixed-size set of working references, e.g. 512 tokens) so per-step latency and memory stay near-constant on multi-page and ultra-long documents. Input: page images (JPG/PNG) or PDFs rendered to images, several pages per request with the prompt '<PAGE><image>' repeated per page plus 'Multi page parsing.'; dynamic tiling ('gundam') or single global view ('base'). Output: text with one <PAGE> marker per page; the SGLang serving caps per-page output at 20,000 tokens and examples use 8,000. OpenAI-compatible chat via SGLang --chat-template unlimited-ocr; no tool calling. MIT license. Hugging Face lists 16 community quantizations usable in llama.cpp, Ollama and LM Studio.

Reasoning is chosen by prefill: <think> enables it, <think></think> answers directly; no enable_thinking kwarg is documented, so thinking_control is absent. kev-0.8b.notes: kev-0.8b: decision model (Kev 1.0, Jared Palmer). Reads a state and answers typed questions (choice / noul / score) with calibrated probabilities in one prefill pass; never generates text, so max_output_tokens is 0 and max_tokens is the serving context (65,536-token state + 8,192 per question row). Held-out index 23.3; new-source accuracy 0.65-0.70. Runs on any Apple silicon or a 4 GB GPU. Measured in AbstractCore on the public dev set (1,328 records): accuracy 0.763, Brier 0.321, ECE 0.030 on MLX bf16, 30 ms per record; about four times faster than Kev-4B on long documents (1.3 s for a 16k-token contract).
